title: KVCache: Sanitizer Shelving & Evictor Probe
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a production capacity event on 2025-01-15 we observed a sustained memory growth in the KV/prefix cache leading to degraded throughput and cascading evictions. Initial mitigation restored service but the post-incident analysis revealed a class of entries that could be 'poisoned' by a combination of concurrent prefetch and eviction race, causing live references to be retained incorrectly and preventing slab reclaim. This ticket captures the follow-ups: a quarantine ("sanitizer shelving") mechanism for suspect cache entries, a synthetic 'evictor probe' harness to reproduce and stress eviction under controlled conditions, telemetry additions to detect poisoning early, and a phased rollout plan for the fixes.
timeline: 2025-01-15 02:18 UTC – First alerts: node p-05 reported memory growth + elevated eviction rate; autoscale initiated
2025-01-15 02:32 UTC – Emergency mitigation: reduced prefetch tunables and introduced short-term eviction-throttle; memory stabilized
2025-01-15 05:00 UTC – Incident declared resolved; team started forensics on heap profiles and cache histograms
2025-01-16 to 2025-01-21 – Reproduction attempts in staging exposed a deterministic window: concurrent prefetch + async compact + eviction = live pointer retention for ~1-2 minutes
2025-01-22 – Root cause hypothesis validated in local harness: a race allowed a retired slab pointer to be re-referenced before tombstone cleanup
2025-01-24 – Initial PR with conservative sanitizer shelving landed behind feature flag (non-default) for canary testing
root_cause_summary: A race between prefetch insertion, async compaction, and eviction created a window where a cache entry could be re-inserted while its previous slab metadata was being compacted. The writepath did not atomically transition the entry to a quarantined state, so stale pointers could survive and be referenced by in-flight requests. Over time, these phantom references prevented memory reclamation and amplified eviction churn.
mitigation: Short-term: reduce prefetch concurrency and enable eviction-throttle during high mem-pressure (rolled out 2025-01-15)
Medium-term: ship sanitizer shelving to quarantine suspect entries when a conflicting transition is detected (this ticket)
Long-term: redesign compact/writepath to use epoch-based reclamation and remove asymmetric state transitions
action_items: ENG-A1: Finish sanitizer shelving implementation behind feature-flag; ensure quarantined entries are scanned and either healed or fast-evicted. Owner: Tomás Rivera. Due: 2025-02-07.

ENG-A2: Build the evictor-probe harness (deterministic eviction/reinsertion simulator) and add to nightly e2e; include presets that match production traffic shape. Owner: Priya Anand. Due: 2025-02-10.

ENG-A3: Add targeted telemetry: tombstone counts, quarantine hits, re-insert-after-compact rate, and histogram of 'time-to-reclaim' per-concurrent-writer. Owner: E2 Observability team (James Liu). Due: 2025-02-01.
ENG-A4: Create an automated test that fuzzes prefetch+compact+evict under different slab sizes; surface regression in CI gating. Owner: QA Automation (Marisol Vega). Due: 2025-02-12.
ENG-A5: Run a staged canary in Dedicated us-west-2 with feature-flag enabled at 5% traffic, monitor quarantine/telemetry signals for 72h, then expand. Owner: SRE (Liam O'Connor). Due: 2025-02-20.
ENG-A6: Postmortem doc update and KB article for on-call runbooks describing how to detect and temporarily mitigate poisoning scenarios. Owner: Incident Lead (Aisha Kapoor). Due: 2025-02-05.
notes: Decision: implement sanitizer shelving as a minimally invasive quarantine that delays reclamation for a short TTL and forces a secondary validation pass; chosen because it reduces blast radius and is reversible.
Trade-off: shelving increases short-term memory by design but prevents long-lived phantom references; TTL default tuned to 90s to match observed window.
Rollback plan: feature-flag + telemetry gates; if quarantine_hit_rate > 0.5% of cache ops with reclaim_time growth > 2x in canary we will revert flag and iterate.
Coordination: schedule a cross-team sync (runtime, obs, QA, SRE) on 2025-02-03 to finalize canary checklist and SLA targets for rollout.
Follow-up research: evaluate epoch-based reclamation (RCU-like) in Q2 as a permanent fix; prototype to be tracked under project kvcache-epoch-reclaim.
